title: Head of Sales Excellence & Methodology
region: San Francisco, CA / New York City, NY
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's sales organization is growing quickly across segments, industries, and geographies, and how we sell has to mature as fast as the team does. We are looking for a Head of Sales Excellence & Methodology to own the substance of sales enablement at Anthropic: the sales methodology itself, the standard for what excellent selling looks like here, and the change management that makes it stick in the field.

You will define a common way of selling that holds up across very different customers, from startups to the largest global enterprises, and then lead the organization through adopting it. That means earning sponsorship from senior sales leadership, equipping frontline managers to coach to the methodology instead of only inspecting for it, and building alongside sellers so the result reflects how deals are really won.

This is a leadership role for someone who has taken a sales organization through real transformation and can show that it changed behavior and results. You will set direction, [build and lead a team], and stay close enough to the field to know when something is not working.

Key responsibilities:

  • Define, document, and evolve Anthropic's sales methodology and process standards, including discovery, qualification, deal strategy, and deal review, so that sellers in every segment and region share a common language

  • Design and run the rollout and reinforcement of methodology changes across the sales organization, securing executive sponsorship and making clear what is expected of each level of sales leadership

  • Equip frontline managers to coach to the methodology in pipeline reviews, deal reviews, and forecasting, so that it becomes part of the operating rhythm

  • Sequence and deliver complex, multi-audience programs across geographies, segments, industries, and roles that scale globally while adapting where local or segment differences matter

  • Develop content, frameworks, and standards together with sellers and sales leaders, testing them on live deals before scaling

  • Define the leading and lagging indicators that show whether the methodology is changing seller behavior and outcomes, and act on what the data shows

  • Partner with Sales Leadership, Revenue Operations, Product, Marketing, and the wider Sales Enablement team so the methodology is reflected in systems, messaging, and day-to-day workflows

  • Apply Claude and internal tooling to personalize coaching and reinforcement, so that quality does not depend on headcount

Minimum qualifications:

  • Practitioner-level expertise in sales methodology and sales process design, including discovery, qualification, deal strategy, deal review, and forecasting

  • Have led a methodology or sales process change across a sales organization, and can show how seller behavior and results changed as a result

  • Have run enablement or sales excellence programs spanning multiple geographies, segments, industries, or roles

  • Have worked directly with senior sales leaders and frontline managers to secure sponsorship for change, including holding a position constructively when they disagreed

  • Have built programs with sellers and sales leaders, testing them on live deals, instead of handing down finished programs

  • Have defined and tracked adoption and impact measures that go beyond completion and satisfaction scores

  • Communicate clearly, in writing and in conversation, with executive audiences

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience building and leading a team of senior enablement or sales excellence professionals

  • A clear, experience-based view of where common sales methodologies break down in practice

  • Prior experience carrying a quota or leading a sales team

  • Experience at an AI company or an enterprise technology company during a period of rapid sales team scaling

  • Hands-on experience using Claude or similar AI tools to automate or personalize coaching and reinforcement

  • Experience selling, or enabling the sale of, complex technical products to both technical and business buyers

$310,000—$360,000 USD

This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

title: Head of Enterprise Risk Management
description:
About the Team

The OpenAI Risk & Audit team is building an enterprise risk capability for a company operating at the frontier of AI. We help leaders identify, understand, and manage the risks that matter most while enabling responsible innovation and durable growth.

We are developing a modern enterprise risk management (ERM) program and the technology foundation that powers it. Our work connects risk strategy, governance, compliance, and assurance with high-quality data, automated workflows, continuous monitoring, and AI-enabled analysis.

We partner across Finance, Security, Legal, Engineering, Product, People, Operations, and Internal Audit, and provide clear reporting to senior leadership and the Board. We aim to make risk ownership practical, decision-useful, and embedded in how OpenAI builds and scales.

About the Role

As the Head of Enterprise Risk Management, you will help build and lead an integrated ERM program and the ERM platform that supports it. You will establish common risk language, governance, and decision processes while translating them into scalable systems, data products, and workflows.

You will own enterprise risk assessments, maintain a centralized risk register, develop risk appetite and key risk indicators, and help leaders evaluate significant changes such as new products, markets, partnerships, major systems, and strategic investments.

This is a senior individual contributor role for a hands-on leader who will build our ERM capability from the ground up, with the potential to build and lead a team over time. You will work with technical and business teams to connect source systems, improve data quality, automate evidence and control monitoring, and use AI to surface emerging risks and accelerate analysis.

You will also help create a strong risk culture, coordinate assurance across the three lines, and communicate complex issues with clarity and sound judgment. This is an opportunity to build a next-generation capability from the ground up.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and evolve OpenAI’s enterprise risk management framework, including risk taxonomy, governance standards, risk appetite, escalation thresholds, and mitigation expectations.

  • Lead enterprise risk assessments and maintain a centralized, decision-useful risk register that reflects strategic, financial, operational, technology, security, compliance, and emerging risks.

  • Establish key risk indicators, continuous-monitoring capabilities, and executive dashboards that translate complex data into clear signals, trends, and actions.

  • Enable risk-informed change governance for new products, markets, partnerships, acquisitions, major systems, and other high-impact initiatives.

  • Lead effective governance forums working cross-functionally with key partners such as Compliance, Finance, Security and others, and prepare concise reporting for senior leadership and the Board.

  • Define the strategy and roadmap for a modern ERM platform that will connect with systems across the enterprise including identity, finance, HR, ticketing, code, and others through reliable integrations and shared data models.

  • Apply automation, policy-as-code, data analytics, and AI-assisted workflows to evidence collection, control monitoring, issue management, risk analysis, and audit or regulatory responses.

  • Coordinate risk activities across Finance, Security, Legal, Compliance, Engineering, Operations, and Internal Audit, clarifying ownership and reducing duplication across the three lines of defense.

  • Build, coach, and lead a high-performing team, strengthen first-line ownership, and foster a culture of practical risk management, curiosity, accountability, and continuous improvement.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 12+ years of experience across enterprise or operational risk, compliance, internal audit, security governance, finance, or related fields, including significant experience leading ERM or GRC programs.

  • A track record of building or materially scaling an enterprise risk program in a fast-growing, technology-driven, or otherwise complex global organization.

  • Strong command of ERM and assurance practices, including risk appetite, risk assessments, KRIs, controls, issue management, and the three-lines model; familiarity with frameworks such as COSO or ISO/IEC 27001/27017/27018/27701/42001.

  • Experience advising executives and presenting risk information to senior governance bodies, with the judgment to make complex tradeoffs clear and actionable.

  • Technical fluency with GRC platforms, data architecture, APIs, system integrations, cloud environments, and automated workflows; experience with infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD, or policy-as-code is a plus.

  • Experience using data analytics, automation, or AI-enabled tools to improve risk sensing, evidence analysis, control monitoring, and reporting.

  • The ability to connect strategic, financial, operational, technology, security, and compliance risks and to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams.

  • Demonstrated success hiring, coaching, and developing multidisciplinary teams while operating effectively in ambiguity and at high velocity.

  • A relevant bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience; credentials such as CIA, CPA, CISA, CRMA, CRM, or an advanced business, legal, or technical degree are valued.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

title: Engineering Manager - Spark
description:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We're looking for Engineering Managers to lead engineering effort on Supabase Spark. Supabase Spark is an initiative to build the next frontier of agentic databases, supporting billions of databases, with millions of databases created every day.

Although we don’t require managers to contribute to code directly, we do expect you to participate in design discussions and to be involved in setting the bar for engineering quality and best practices.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

Team & People

  • Build a healthy, high-trust team culture in a remote-first, globally distributed environment.

  • Run 1:1s, performance management, career development, and onboarding for your direct reports.

  • Handle people admin (leave, time off, etc.) for your team.

Hiring

  • Own the hiring plan for your team and act as Hiring Manager. First round of interviewer for all roles on the team.

  • Partner with Talent Acquisition to source, interview, and close strong candidates.

  • Contribute to headcount planning, org design, and the evolution of engineering leadership at Supabase.

Delivery & Roadmap

  • Own the team's roadmap and project management (Linear), driving accountability and clear milestones.

  • Manage workflow intake and Slack triage. These are the team’s primary inboxes for cross-team requests. You decide what gets routed where, prioritized, or pushed back on.

  • Own the team's weekly updates and keep stakeholders aligned without creating overhead.

  • Organize effort against support tickets and maintain the team's SLO.

  • Surface risks, dependencies, and tradeoffs early and clearly to leadership.

Incident Commander

  • Train as an Incident Commander. Drive coordination, resolution, and post-incident follow-up.

  • Lead blameless post-incident reviews

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

  • Have 5+ years of engineering background, with enough depth to be credible with engineers building complex systems.

  • Have 3+ years managing remote engineering teams.

  • Have managed engineering teams at a cloud, SaaS, or developer tools company.

  • Experience with developer tools or databases, plus if that includes both SQLite and Postgres ecosystems.

  • Strong technical credibility in backend and database systems: APIs, auth, and Postgres access control (roles, grants, RLS) etc.

  • Has led a team shipping a developer facing API or platform product from early stage to production.

  • Have managed remote, globally distributed teams that work asynchronously across disparate time zones.

  • Are technical enough to be credible with strong engineers, but genuinely passionate about people management. This is the work you want to do, not a track you're settling for.

  • Build psychological safety and a feedback culture: you give feedback often and in the moment, ask for it back, and create space for the team to do the same.

  • Operate as a multiplier. Focused on helping individuals achieve more than they could alone, not on being the best technical voice in the room.

  • Coach rather than direct. Remove blockers, connect people to context and resources, and trust your engineers to own how the work gets done.

  • Have a real track record of performance management and can speak to specific examples of difficult conversations and how you navigated them.

  • Are comfortable with ambiguity and capable of building structure where there isn't much.

  • Communicate clearly and write well. You're default async, default written, set context proactively, and surface risks early.

  • Are collaborative, low-ego, and adaptable. You thrive working with high-autonomy, senior ICs who have strong technical opinions and don't need to be the smartest person in the room.

  • Are comfortable with aggressive scoping and eval driven development.

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

title: Head of Business Development, LATAM
description:

The Head of Business Development, LATAM will lead OpenAI’s regional BD strategy and execution. You will serve as the single-threaded point of contact for regional leadership across the full Business Development organization, setting priorities and coordinating the teams needed to deliver them.

The scope includes growth (consumer and SMB), plugins and MCP, search, commerce, B2B marketplaces, and ads/monetization partnerships. You will identify priorities, originate and lead deals, manage key partner relationships, and work with global program owners on deals and initiatives across these areas.

This is a senior, hands-on role based in São Paulo. As the first dedicated LATAM BD hire, you will personally lead complex deals, work closely with Product, Engineering, Finance and GTM/Sales, and build the team as resources become available. Success requires great judgment, product orientation, and consistent execution from negotiation through launch and ongoing performance.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own the LATAM BD plan. Agree on priorities with regional and country leadership, identify where partnerships can materially improve outcomes, and allocate effort across markets and programs.

title: Head of New Media
description:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

Traditional PR is fading — we go directly to our audience. This role brings together what used to be two separate seats, communications and social media, into one mid-to-senior, hands-on role: owning Supabase's voice in the channels where developers actually pay attention, and building our founders' presence in them.

"New media" here means modern and direct, not traditional press — we care far more about getting our founders onto the right podcasts and YouTube channels than landing a New York Times placement. It's part comms, part social operator, with a sharper edge than a typical polite PR hire: someone willing to put an opinion out there and push a little rather than always play it safe. But it's not just a social media job either — this person also needs the poise and technical credibility to lead comms through genuinely high-stakes moments, like a major incident, where reporters, investors, and customers all need a calm, credible, technically fluent voice at the same time.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

  • Make sure we're part of the current conversation and are going directly to our audience — new media over old-world press

  • Own and execute our new media strategy

    • Run and grow Supabase's X + LinkedIn accounts, hands on keyboard

    • Help build the accounts of our founders and team — including ghostwriting in their voice

    • Explore and exploit unconventional channels and formats

    • Book our cofounders on the most known shows, podcasts, and YouTube channels in our space

  • Work directly with DevRel and the PMM team on launches and Select

  • Manage comms around incidents, funding, and other high-stakes moments — crisis comms handled with poise and technical credibility (this is key)

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

  • Are an excellent writer with a distinctive voice — equally strong posting as yourself and ghostwriting for others

  • Have a track record of growing accounts, ideally for a technical audience

  • Unconventional thinker — willing to put an opinion out there and push a little, with the judgment to know when

  • Seasoned enough for the serious moments — incidents, funding, press — calm, credible, and technically fluent

  • High agency — you're probably already doing a version of this somewhere scrappier

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

  • 60+ countries

  • 20+ languages spoken

  • Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

  • 540,000+ community members

title: Sales Manager, Enterprise Industries
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Sales Manager, Enterprise Industries

As a Sales Manager at Anthropic, you'll lead a team of Enterprise Account Executives driving the adoption of safe, frontier AI by securing strategic deals with leading enterprises. You'll leverage your leadership and consultative sales expertise in the Industries sector to propel revenue growth while developing a high-performing team of AEs. Working closely with Applied AI Engineering and Product teams, you'll help Industries customers embed and deploy AI while uncovering its full range of capabilities across their business. In collaboration with GTM and Marketing teams, you'll continuously refine our value proposition, sales methodology, and market positioning to resonate with enterprise decision-makers and ensure differentiated value across the Industries landscape.

The ideal candidate will have a passion for developing people, identifying market opportunities within Industries, and executing strategies to capture them. By leading the deployment of Anthropic's emerging products, you will help enterprises obtain new capabilities while also advancing the ethical development of AI.

Responsibilities:

  • Build and lead a high-performing team of Enterprise Account Executives focused on Industries, providing coaching, mentorship, and guidance to drive team success
  • Develop and implement sales strategies tailored to Industries procurement cycles and budgeting processes to meet and exceed team revenue quotas
  • Create and maintain accurate forecasts, pipeline management, and reporting while ensuring data integrity in CRM systems
  • Partner with Enablement to develop training programs and resources that accelerate AE ramp time and effectiveness, with specific focus on Industries buying cycles and decision-making processes
  • Work closely with Applied AI Engineering teams to demonstrate technical capabilities pre-sales and optimize solutions post-sales for industry-specific applications
  • Enable your team to have credible technical conversations about AI applications in Industries while maintaining appropriate guardrails
  • Build strong partnerships across the organization to drive strategic initiatives within the Industries sector
  • Identify and execute on new market opportunities and use cases for Anthropic's AI solutions across business units, research and development centers, and corporate functions
  • Help your team navigate complex enterprise stakeholder ecosystems including executives, business leaders, IT departments, and procurement offices to build consensus
  • Gather and synthesize customer feedback to inform product direction and enhance customer experience for Industries
  • Build and continuously refine the Industries sales methodology by incorporating learnings into playbooks and best practices

You may be a good fit if you have:

  • 15+ years of enterprise sales experience in Industries technology, preferably driving adoption of SaaS or emerging technologies
  • 5+ years of sales leadership experience, ideally 3+ leading teams within the Enterprise segment focused on Industries in France
  • Proven track record of building and leading high-performing sales teams selling into large enterprises, with demonstrated success in coaching and developing AEs
  • Experience establishing and scaling sales processes, tools, and methodologies in fast-growing organizations serving Industries
  • Strong technical acumen and ability to understand complex AI solutions and their applications in Industries, with experience enabling teams to have credible technical conversations with customer stakeholders
  • Track record of successful partnership with technical teams throughout the customer journey within large enterprises
  • Deep understanding of Industries buying cycles, procurement frameworks, and key pain points
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate complex, multithreaded sales cycles across diverse stakeholder groups and drive cross-functional initiatives
  • Experience managing complex enterprise sales cycles and helping AEs secure strategic deals
  • Strong operational rigor in pipeline management, forecasting, and sales metrics specific to Industries sales cycles
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to build relationships across all levels, from technical and business teams to senior executives in Industries
  • Strategic approach to market analysis combined with tactical excellence in execution
  • Passion for AI technology and commitment to its safe, responsible development

Sales Manager, Enterprise Industries

En tant que Sales Manager chez Anthropic, vous dirigerez une équipe d'Enterprise Account Executives qui favorise l'adoption d'une IA de pointe et sûre en concluant des contrats stratégiques avec des entreprises de premier plan. Vous mettrez à profit votre leadership et votre expertise de la vente consultative dans le secteur Industries pour accélérer la croissance du chiffre d'affaires, tout en développant une équipe d'AE très performante. En étroite collaboration avec les équipes Applied AI Engineering et Produit, vous aiderez les clients Industries à intégrer et à déployer l'IA, tout en leur faisant découvrir l'étendue de ses capacités dans l'ensemble de leurs activités. En collaboration avec les équipes GTM et Marketing, vous affinerez en continu notre proposition de valeur, notre méthodologie de vente et notre positionnement, afin qu'ils trouvent un écho auprès des instances décisionnelles des grandes entreprises et apportent une valeur différenciée sur l'ensemble du secteur Industries.

Le profil idéal a à cœur de faire grandir ses équipes, de repérer les opportunités de marché au sein du secteur Industries et de mettre en œuvre les stratégies qui permettent de les saisir. En pilotant le déploiement des produits émergents d'Anthropic, vous aiderez les entreprises à acquérir de nouvelles capacités tout en contribuant au développement éthique de l'IA.

Responsabilités :

  • Constituer et diriger une équipe très performante d'Enterprise Account Executives dédiée au secteur Industries, en lui apportant coaching, mentorat et accompagnement pour assurer sa réussite
  • Élaborer et mettre en œuvre des stratégies commerciales adaptées aux cycles d'achat et aux processus budgétaires du secteur Industries, afin d'atteindre et de dépasser les objectifs de chiffre d'affaires de l'équipe
  • Établir et tenir à jour des prévisions fiables, assurer la gestion du pipeline et le reporting, tout en garantissant l'intégrité des données dans les systèmes CRM
  • Travailler avec l'équipe Enablement pour concevoir des programmes de formation et des ressources qui accélèrent la montée en compétence et l'efficacité des AE, avec une attention particulière aux cycles d'achat et aux processus de décision du secteur Industries
  • Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes Applied AI Engineering pour démontrer les capacités techniques en avant-vente et optimiser les solutions en après-vente pour les applications propres à chaque secteur
  • Permettre à votre équipe de mener des échanges techniques crédibles sur les applications de l'IA dans le secteur Industries, dans le respect des garde-fous appropriés
  • Nouer des partenariats solides au sein de l'organisation pour faire avancer les initiatives stratégiques du secteur Industries
  • Identifier et concrétiser de nouvelles opportunités de marché et de nouveaux cas d'usage pour les solutions d'IA d'Anthropic au sein des directions métiers, des centres de recherche et développement et des fonctions support
  • Aider votre équipe à naviguer dans des écosystèmes complexes de parties prenantes au sein des grandes entreprises (direction générale, directions métiers, DSI et services achats) afin de construire un consensus
  • Recueillir et synthétiser les retours des clients pour éclairer l'orientation produit et améliorer l'expérience client du secteur Industries
  • Construire et affiner en continu la méthodologie de vente Industries en intégrant les enseignements dans des playbooks et des bonnes pratiques

Ce poste pourrait vous correspondre si vous avez :

  • Au moins 15 ans d'expérience en vente aux grands comptes dans les technologies pour le secteur Industries, de préférence dans l'adoption de solutions SaaS ou de technologies émergentes
  • Au moins 5 ans d'expérience en management commercial, dont idéalement 3 ans ou plus à la tête d'équipes du segment Enterprise dédiées au secteur Industries en France
  • Une expérience confirmée de la constitution et de la direction d'équipes commerciales très performantes vendant aux grandes entreprises, avec des réussites avérées dans le coaching et le développement des AE
  • Une expérience de la mise en place et du déploiement à grande échelle de processus, d'outils et de méthodologies de vente dans des organisations en forte croissance au service du secteur Industries
  • Une solide culture technique et la capacité à comprendre des solutions d'IA complexes et leurs applications dans le secteur Industries, ainsi que l'habitude de préparer vos équipes à mener des échanges techniques crédibles avec les parties prenantes côté client
  • Une expérience réussie de la collaboration avec les équipes techniques tout au long du parcours client au sein de grandes entreprises
  • Une connaissance approfondie des cycles d'achat, des cadres de passation des marchés et des principales problématiques du secteur Industries
  • Une capacité avérée à piloter des cycles de vente complexes impliquant de multiples interlocuteurs et des parties prenantes variées, et à mener des initiatives transverses
  • Une expérience de la gestion de cycles de vente complexes aux grands comptes et de l'accompagnement des AE dans la conclusion de contrats stratégiques
  • Une grande rigueur opérationnelle dans la gestion du pipeline, les prévisions et les indicateurs commerciaux propres aux cycles de vente du secteur Industries
  • D'excellentes compétences en communication et la capacité à nouer des relations à tous les niveaux, des équipes techniques et métiers jusqu'aux membres de la direction du secteur Industries
  • Une approche stratégique de l'analyse de marché, alliée à une exécution tactique irréprochable
  • Un intérêt marqué pour les technologies d'IA et un engagement en faveur de leur développement sûr et responsable



Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

title: Global Head of Education GTM
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to build safe artificial general intelligence that benefits all of humanity. Our Go To Market team helps customers understand, adopt, and deploy AI, bringing together Sales, Solutions, Support, Marketing, and Partnerships.

Our education work spans higher education, country-level partnerships, and K–12 teachers. We help institutions and students build durable AI capabilities for the future and explore how AI can support teaching, learning, research, and institutional operations.

About the Role

We are seeking a Head of Global Education GTM to lead our education partnerships & sales, shape GTM strategy, and scale the team for its next stage of growth. You will set priorities across markets and customer segments, lead representatives and regional management, and stay close to complex opportunities and senior customer relationships.

This is a strategic, hands-on leadership role at the intersection of partnerships, product, and adoption. You will help the team move customers from experimentation to responsible, sustained use of frontier AI. Seats and meaningful capability building and adoption are the primary goals, alongside disciplined management of the team’s commercial responsibilities.

You will lead technical, consultative Account Directors who own the customer journey from territory strategy and pipeline creation through use case identification, evaluation, procurement, deployment, adoption, consumption, value realization, and expansion. Your judgment will help the team connect executive ambition with credible technical and training plans as well as institutional readiness.

You are a strategic thinker who is comfortable speaking with leaders on the future of AI in education, and shaping GTM while technology and capabilities are still being built. Education experience is welcome but not required; we are looking for a strategic technology sales leader with strong learning agility, product sense, scrappiness, and mission alignment. International experience is helpful but not required.

In this role, you will:

  • Define and execute a global education GTM strategy across higher education, country-level partnerships, and K–12 teachers, making clear choices about segments, markets, and resource allocation.

  • Lead, coach, and develop Account Directors and regional management, building the hiring plan and management capacity needed to scale.

  • Stay hands-on with major opportunities, helping the team navigate executive alignment, decentralized stakeholders, technical evaluation, governance, procurement, and deployment.

  • Develop trusted relationships with institutional leaders, education systems, country-level stakeholders, and partners.

  • Build repeatable sales and partnership approaches that expand seats and support sustained adoption and value realization.

  • Establish territory planning, pipeline reviews, forecasting, and account management that connect adoption goals with subscription and consumption responsibilities.

  • Partner with Product, technical teams, Marketing, Strategy and Operations, and other functions to shape credible customer plans and inform product priorities.

  • Help institutions build faculty and educator AI capabilities, connecting access with practical use and learning.

  • Guide the team through product change and ambiguity, distinguishing available capabilities from dependencies that require validation.

We’re seeking someone with:

  • A track record of leading and developing sales teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and building repeatable operating practices.

  • Strong strategic judgment: the ability to make explicit tradeoffs, prioritize opportunities, and translate a long-term vision into frontline execution.

  • Experience leading complex enterprise technology sales or partnerships involving executive, technical, operational, and procurement stakeholders.

  • Strong product sense and technical curiosity, with the ability to learn evolving AI capabilities and partner effectively with technical experts.

  • Evidence of building in ambiguous, rapidly changing environments with limited resources, incomplete processes, or products still evolving.

  • A customer-centered approach that extends through deployment, adoption, usage, and expansion.

  • Clear communication and cross-functional influence across senior leaders, specialists, and frontline teams.

  • A mission-driven interest in expanding access to AI and helping educators and institutions build durable capability.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Are a strategist who makes difficult choices and brings teams along with a clear rationale.

  • Are a builder who creates systems and teams while staying willing to do the frontline work.

  • Enjoy learning new technology and translating it into practical customer opportunities.

  • Can move between an executive conversation, a deal review, and a discussion about deployment readiness.

  • Measure progress through meaningful customer use and can balance mission, adoption, and commercial discipline.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

title: Head of Digital Natives & Startups, ANZ
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

We are seeking a Head of Digital Natives & Startups, ANZ to build and lead Anthropic's go-to-market motion for digital native businesses and startups across Australia and New Zealand. You will grow a team that wins and expands the region's fastest-moving, AI-forward companies, driving consumption of Claude directly and through our cloud partners. You will set the segment strategy, hire and develop the team, and work closely with Product, Partnerships and Marketing to turn ANZ builders into long-term customers. This is a chance to shape how one of the world's most dynamic startup ecosystems adopts frontier AI, while representing ANZ's priorities to our global leadership.

Key responsibilities

  • Define and execute the ANZ go-to-market strategy for Digital Natives and Startups, covering both new customer acquisition and growth within existing accounts
  • Build, hire and lead a high-performing sales team across Australia and New Zealand, with clear targets, regular coaching and defined career paths
  • Own pipeline, forecast and consumption targets for the segment, running a consumption-based sales motion
  • Build a repeatable motion across the customer lifecycle, from early-stage founders to scaled, high-growth digital natives
  • Develop strong relationships across the ANZ startup ecosystem, including founders, venture investors, accelerators and developer communities
  • Partner with cloud providers and our Partnerships team to co-sell and extend our reach in the segment
  • Collaborate with Product, Marketing, Solutions and Customer Success to adapt our offering and messaging for ANZ, and bring customer feedback back to the business
  • Represent ANZ priorities to regional and global leadership, and keep local execution aligned with global strategy
  • Act as an executive sponsor for key customers and communicate Anthropic's trust and safety principles with credibility

Minimum qualifications

  • 15+ years of overall experience selling technology products to enterprise organisations across ANZ market
  • 5+ years of people management experience leading sales teams in the digital native and/or startup segment
  • Proven success in consumption-based technology sales, such as cloud, API or usage-based SaaS
  • Experience building a business or team from the ground up in Australia and/or New Zealand
  • Track record across both customer acquisition and account growth
  • Strong network and credibility in the ANZ startup and digital native ecosystem
  • Ability to explain technical products clearly to founders, engineers and executives

Preferred qualifications

  • Background at Google, AWS or a similar cloud or SaaS company
  • Experience selling AI, machine learning or developer-focused products
  • Experience co-selling with cloud partners and working with channel
  • Experience hiring and scaling a team through rapid growth
  • Familiarity with the ANZ regulatory and data-privacy landscape

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

title: Head of AI Native Operations
description:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role
We are looking for a Head of AI Native Operations to build the autonomous systems that run Supabase.

Supabase is building an AI-native internal operating system, where agents carry the operational load end to end. We are standing up a new central team to build that platform and run it in production. This is the role that leads it, and it is hands-on. You design the architecture, build the first versions of the critical pieces, and are accountable for whether every agent we run is correct, safe, and improving over time. We build rather than buy, and there are no settled best practices for most of this yet, so you will be setting them.

You will lead a team of senior individual contributors extending the platform and driving adoption across teams.

What You’ll Be Responsible For
In this role, you’ll:

  • Own the agent platform architecture: The harness and orchestration layer and connectors into company systems, shared context and memory, and the path from prototype to production.

  • Catch regressions before they ship: Model, prompt, and tool changes can’t ship until they pass the evals. When a new model comes out, you know within hours whether to adopt it.

  • Make every agent observable: Every run and every decision is traced. For any agent at any time, you can answer what it did, why, what it cost, and how its quality is trending.

  • Own safety and trust: Design the controls that let agents act without a human in the loop: least-privilege credentials, hard policy limits, escalation thresholds, audit logs, sandboxing, and prompt-injection defenses.

  • Replace workflows, don’t assist them: Pick the workflows agents can fully own today and take them to production.

  • Turn wins into a platform: Package what works into reusable components, templates, and eval harnesses so other teams can ship their own production agents without starting from scratch.

  • Build and direct the team: Hire and grow senior ICs, review their designs and pull requests, and hold the quality bar.

  • Measure what matters: Track workflows automated, eval pass rates, cost per run, and work absorbed against the hiring plan.



How You’ll Think

A Point of View on Where Automation Wins
You have a thesis about how AI and automation change the way a company operates, and it comes from building, not reading. You can look at a business and say which workflows agents can own today, which they will own in 12 months as models improve, and which still need people, and why. You defend that view with evidence from systems you have shipped, and you update it when the evals tell you to.

Eval-Driven
You don’t trust an agent because the demo looked good. You trust it because it passes a test set of real cases, and you know which cases it fails. When anything changes, your first question is “what do the evals say?”

Inversion Thinking
Left alone, an autonomous system tends to fail quietly, or people route around it. So the first question about any agent isn’t “does it work on the happy path?” but “how will this break, and how will we know?” The design follows from that answer: what the agent is never allowed to do, what it escalates, and which alert fires when quality drifts.

Recursive Thinking
Every system you build should produce the evidence that grades it. An agent isn’t done when it works. It’s done when it tells you, without you in the loop, that it has stopped working.

Must Have

  • Hands-on agent building: Have personally designed and built autonomous agent or LLM systems that ran in production and that others depended on. Prototypes, demos, and configuring a vendor tool don’t count. You don’t need to be a career software engineer, but you must have built these systems yourself.

  • Architecture depth: Can explain how the pieces fit together (orchestration, tool and data access, context and memory, tracing, evals, guardrails, deployment), with opinions on current frameworks.

  • Security judgment: Have shipped agents that take real actions with real permissions, and designed the controls that made that safe.

  • A tested point of view: Can argue, with examples from your own builds, where autonomous systems create real business leverage and where they don’t yet.

  • Technical leadership: Have led senior builders and set the quality bar through design and code review.

Strong Signal

  • Have replaced a human-run business workflow (finance, operations, support, release management) end to end with an autonomous system.

  • Are native to Git, Markdown, and pull requests, and comfortable reading and writing Python or TypeScript.

  • Have taken an internal platform from zero to adoption by teams you did not control.

  • A software engineering background is a plus, but not required.

What Success Looks Like

  • Six months: 20+ autonomous agents in production on the shared platform, each with an eval suite, tracing, and a named owner.

  • Regressions get caught, not discovered: Quality problems surface in an alert or dashboard before a user reports them.

  • Workflows replaced, not assisted: Multiple high-volume workflows are fully owned by agents, with humans handling only escalations.

  • Trusted by default: No agent causes material financial, security, or customer harm, and every agent’s permissions and actions can be audited.

  • Teams ship their own: At least three teams outside the core team run production agents built on the platform.

  • Autonomous team: Your two reports work independently, and you spend your time on architecture and review rather than execution.

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

  • ~400 team members

  • 60+ countries

  • 20+ languages spoken

  • Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

  • 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

title: Engineering Manager, ChatGPT Space
description:
About the Team

The ChatGPT Space team is rethinking what work looks like when teams and agents can create together. We are building a shared workspace where a rough idea can become a polished, editable artifact, from Pages, Sheets, and Slides to entirely new kinds of work products.

Our ambition is to build the best place for teams and agents to turn ideas into things they could not make alone. The work should keep evolving after the first draft, drawing on shared context, improving through collaboration, and staying current as a project moves forward.

This is a high-agency team working across product, design, and research. We partner closely with model training teams to shape how frontier models create and edit artifacts, then bring those capabilities into a coherent experience across Pages, files, and tools. The work spans full-stack product engineering, editing and rendering systems, model integration, and collaboration, with a high bar for taste, correctness, and speed.

About the Role

As Engineering Manager, ChatGPT Space, you will lead and grow the product engineering team defining this experience. You will help shape both the product and the team that builds it, turning an ambitious, evolving vision into software people love to use.

You will partner with product and design on what great collaboration between teams and agents should feel like, with research on what models can create, and with infrastructure and enterprise partners on a dependable experience at scale.

This is a role for a leader who has built from zero to one and wants to help define a new category of work. You will bring the technical depth to guide hard decisions and the product judgment to know what is worth building, while developing engineers and giving them the clarity and autonomy to ship.

This role is based in San Francisco.

In this role, you will

  • Lead, manage, and grow a product engineering team, creating clear ownership, supporting engineers’ development, and hiring exceptional people

  • Partner with product and design to shape the ChatGPT Space roadmap and translate user needs into focused, well-crafted releases

  • Lead the development of creation, editing, and collaboration experiences for teams and agents, including tools that connect project context and keep work up to date

  • Set technical direction for full-stack product systems, editing and rendering surfaces, and model-facing integrations

  • Partner closely with research teams on artifact tools, model behavior, training needs, and evaluations, turning improvements in model capability into better products

  • Establish a high bar for editor quality, correctness, latency, and reliability, and use user feedback and evaluation results to guide improvements

  • Work with infrastructure and enterprise partners to deliver dependable experiences, align interfaces and ownership, and resolve problems across team boundaries

  • Balance new product development with the technical investments and operational discipline needed to sustain quality as the product grows

  • Build an effective operating cadence that keeps a fast-moving team aligned and gives engineers the context and autonomy to do their best work

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Have a track record of leading engineering teams and helping engineers grow while delivering excellent products

  • Have built products from zero to one and can turn an ambiguous opportunity into a clear direction and practical execution plan

  • Bring strong product judgment and design taste, with a deep interest in how teams and agents create, edit, and collaborate

  • Have strong full-stack engineering fundamentals and can guide technical decisions across frontend, backend, and model-facing systems

  • Work effectively with product, design, research, and infrastructure partners, building alignment without losing momentum

  • Care deeply about craft, performance, correctness, and reliability, and can help a team improve all four while moving quickly

  • Communicate clearly, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and adapt as user needs and model capabilities evolve

  • Want to help define and build a new category of work for teams and agents

Experience as a founder, product manager, or design engineer would be especially relevant, as would a track record of bringing a similarly strong product perspective to engineering leadership.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

title: Marketing Manager, Partnerships
description:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

*Titles posted to our careers page are updated regularly to best advertise the role and expected seniority, but internally we have a flat titling system with two types of titles: one for individual contributors and one for people managers.

About the Role

Runway is looking for a Marketing Manager to help build and scale high-impact marketing programs across our creator, partner, sponsorship, and growth ecosystem.

This is a generalist marketing role for someone who can move fluidly between strategy and execution. Some immediate areas of focus include influencer creator partnerships, sponsorships, and partnership marketing.

The right person is commercially minded, highly organized, creative, and comfortable operating in ambiguity. We are looking for someone who can build repeatable programs, manage relationships, and execute campaigns to turn marketing ideas into measurable growth.

What You’ll Do

  • You will own and support marketing programs that help Runway reach priority audiences, grow demand, and deepen our presence among our target audiences.

  • In the near term, this will include managing creator and influencer partnerships including affiliates, evaluating sponsorship opportunities, and building co-marketing programs with customers, technology partners, model providers, vendors, and ecosystem partners.

  • You will work across the full program lifecycle: identifying opportunities, developing briefs, managing outreach, coordinating execution, tracking performance, and recommending what to scale, change, or stop.

  • You will partner closely with growth, creative, comms, events, PMM, sales, business development, legal, and finance to make sure programs are clear, on-brand, operationally sound, and connected to business outcomes.

What We’re Looking For

  • We’re looking for a marketing generalist with strong executional judgment and enough strategic range to work across multiple types of programs for a range of B2C and B2B audiences.

  • Experience managing creator partnerships with a clear view of how long-form content performs differently from short-form and other social channels.

  • 4+ years of experience building marketing campaigns, influencer, affiliate, or growth programs from 0 to 1.

  • Experience managing external relationships: creators, sponsors, agencies, freelancers or vendors.

  • Experience writing briefs, managing timelines, coordinating stakeholders, and translating broad goals into concrete plans.

  • Strong taste, communication skills, and judgment around brand, audience fit, creator quality, partner value, business impact, and operational tradeoffs.

  • You should be comfortable with ambiguity and able to build from scratch. This role requires someone who can create structure where it does not yet exist, but without slowing the team down with unnecessary process.

  • You should care about measurement and be able to connect marketing programs to outcomes such as subscriptions, ARR, and enterprise pipeline influence.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in AI, SaaS, subscription products.

  • Experience creating partner-facing materials such as briefs, sponsorship packages, or co-marketing materials.

  • Familiarity with Runway, AI video, creator communities, internet culture, and the broader creative technology ecosystem.

Runway strives to recruit and retain exceptional talent from diverse backgrounds while ensuring pay equity for our team. Our salary ranges are based on competitive market rates for our size, stage and industry, and salary is just one part of the overall compensation package we provide.

There are many factors that go into salary determinations, including relevant experience, skill level and qualifications assessed during the interview process, and maintaining internal equity with peers on the team. The range shared below is a general expectation for the function as posted, but we are also open to considering candidates who may be more or less experienced than outlined in the job description. In this case, we will communicate any updates in the expected salary range.

Lastly, the provided range is the expected salary for candidates in the U.S. Outside of those regions, there may be a change in the range, which again, will be communicated to candidates.

Working at Runway

Great things come from great teams. We’d love to hear from you.

We’re committed to creating a space where our employees can bring their full selves to work and have equal opportunity to succeed. So regardless of race, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, origin, ability, age, veteran status, if joining this mission speaks to you, we encourage you to apply.

title: Head of Sourcing Enablement & Delivery
description:
About the Team

Strategic Sourcing & Procurement helps OpenAI secure the products, services, and partnerships that support our research, build our products, and grow our business. We work with teams across the company to make sound commercial decisions and move important work forward.

As OpenAI grows, we are rethinking how sourcing works: bringing expertise into decisions earlier, simplifying contracting, and using AI to give Procurement more time for judgment and strategic work. What we learn internally—and through our supplier and enterprise-buyer relationships—can also inform better products, partnerships, and industry adoption.

About the Role

We’re looking for a senior leader to head Sourcing Enablement & Delivery, leading sourcing operational delivery, contracting enablement, and AI transformation—and building Procurement’s contribution to OpenAI’s commercial growth. You will build the teams, systems, service model, and cross-functional partnerships that enable sourcing and contracting at scale, helping teams move quickly without losing commercial discipline or accountability.

You will partner with GTM, Sales, and Partnerships to develop Procurement’s contribution to OpenAI adoption and commercial growth. Bring procurement-industry knowledge, buyer insights, and lessons from internal AI use into customer engagement, product feedback, and opportunities across the procurement ecosystem.

Reporting to the Head of Strategic Sourcing, you will manage the Sourcing Delivery and Contract Management leaders and shape this new function’s priorities, team, and measures of success.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

Priorities and what success looks like

  • A focused roadmap: clear choices about what to build first, what to defer, and how progress will be measured.

  • Stronger delivery: capable leaders and teams, faster execution, less rework, and fewer unresolved ownership gaps.

  • AI adoption: sustained use of AI-enabled capabilities, with measurable gains in quality, capacity, and user experience.

  • Commercial results: increased OpenAI adoption across the procurement industry and a measurable contribution to commercial growth, consistent with independent supplier selection and purchasing decisions.

In this role, you will:

  • Build and lead the organization. Hire and develop managers, coach performance, and build succession and leadership depth. Decide how employees, contractors, delivery partners, and AI share the work. Hold leaders accountable for results, capacity, and team health.

  • Own sourcing enablement and delivery operations. Set service commitments and quality standards with the Delivery and Contract Management leaders. Match support to deal complexity and risk, and use internal customer feedback to improve the service. Category and Sourcing leads retain ownership of their strategies and deals, including supplier selection, negotiations, and purchasing.

  • Lead the sourcing operating rhythm. Bring demand, priorities, and capacity into one forward plan, informed by workload and performance data. Work with category leaders to make tradeoffs, resolve dependencies, and follow through on commitments. Provide inputs to Procurement-wide planning and functional business reviews.

  • Strengthen contracting. Partner with Legal and Procurement Operations/COE on contract lifecycle management, approved templates, and negotiation playbooks that improve quality and free category teams to focus on strategic deals.

  • Lead RACI development. Define responsibilities, decision rights, handoffs, and escalation paths within Procurement and across partner teams. Define how the team prioritizes work, allocates resources, and resolves delivery issues.

  • Create mechanisms to bring sourcing into decisions earlier: connect business demand, supplier activity, and renewals—including work outside formal intake—with Sourcing teams, so options can be shaped before commitments and Finance and cross-functional teams can have better visibility.

  • Build and prove AI-enabled ways of working. Own use-case priorities, adoption, and business outcomes for sourcing and contracting experiences that begin in ChatGPT and connect to trusted enterprise systems. Partner with Finance Enterprise Technology on technical delivery and with Legal, Security, and Operations on controls and support, including preserving access restrictions and contractual commitments. Turn what works into reusable capabilities, demonstrations, and product feedback.

  • Define Procurement’s commercial-enablement approach with GTM, Partnerships, Legal, and Compliance including program scope, decision rights, purchasing independence, and information-sharing boundaries. Lead Procurement’s analysis, coordination, and follow-through for approved programs; GTM owns customer sales. Maintain independent purchasing decision-making and identify and escalate any proposed linkage between OpenAI’s purchasing commitments and customer sales.

  • Help define goals and measures of success for Procurement’s contribution to OpenAI adoption and commercial growth with Sourcing leadership and cross-functional partners.

  • Bring procurement-buyer expertise into GTM. Own this team’s buyer insights and use cases. Work with Marketing, Sales, Product, Customer Success, and Partnerships to shape demonstrations, industry content, and customer conversations, using examples approved for external use.

  • Drive OpenAI adoption across the procurement industry. Work with Sourcing leadership, partners and GTM to explore how Procurement third-parties and partners can adopt and distribute OpenAI capabilities. Contribute industry expertise and evidence from internal use; GTM and Partnerships own commercialization.

  • Partner with Legal and Compliance to embed business-integrity and confidentiality safeguards; implement required disclosures, recusals, and independent-decision making arrangements.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 12+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, vendor management, or commercial leadership, with strong judgment about supplier choices, negotiations, contracts, and risk.

  • Have built or transformed a procurement capability through rapid growth or change, with clear evidence of better execution, commercial outcomes, or user experience.

  • Have managed managers and developed strong teams through hiring, coaching, performance management, succession planning, and thoughtful use of internal and external capacity.

  • Have worked in or closely with marketing, sales, or commercial teams, ideally serving procurement buyers. You can turn customer needs into use cases and business cases, and deliver commercial results with partner teams.

  • Know the procurement industry—its buyers, technology providers, service firms, and buying priorities. You understand how to sell to Procurement, including how buyers assess risk, negotiate, and secure internal support.

  • Use industry analysts, market research, buyer conversations, and professional networks to form a point of view on emerging trends and inform roadmaps, partnerships, and GTM priorities.

  • Have turned AI, automation, or enterprise technology into capabilities people use. You can work with technical partners, drive adoption, measure improvements, and recognize where human judgment remains essential.

  • Can set direction when the path is not defined. You prioritize work and resources, explain tradeoffs plainly, and earn support from teams you do not manage. You are curious about AI and willing to test, learn, and change course.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

About the role

This role sits within the AWS partnership team and drives Supabase's and AWS's joint co-marketing and GTM motion in support of segments like gaming, enterprise, startups, and AI.

You'll work closely with the segment leads driving each motion and with the Alliances Lead, translating segment strategy into the campaigns and content that actually reach AWS field teams and partners.

  • Produce co-marketing content and enablement assets (case studies, campaign materials, partner-facing documentation) for our gaming, enterprise, startup, and AI segments

  • Plan and execute joint campaigns with AWS field and marketing teams, from initial concept through launch

  • Support AWS-funded marketing engagements and executive-facing events with content and coordination

  • Build and maintain enablement materials that keep our partner-facing teams and AWS contacts current on Supabase's story

  • Identify the right audiences and contacts for campaigns, partnering with RevOps and marketing tooling as needed

Who you are

  • 3-5+ years in partner marketing or co-marketing, ideally with experience working alongside a major cloud provider like AWS or similar strategic partner

  • Strong writer and communicator, able to turn technical products and partnerships into clear, compelling narratives

  • Execution-oriented. This role is about shipping campaigns and content, not managing a mature, fully-staffed program

  • High degree of autonomy and external credibility. You lead your own workstreams, close loops, and represent Supabase in high-stakes partner discussions independently

  • Experience with AWS Partner Central, ACE, and Marketplace mechanisms is a plus

What We Offer

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

About the Team
